context: It contained 258 full-page miniature paintings by the leading masters of the Tabriz school, including the great **Sultan Muhammad** (one of the most influential Persian painters of any era), and the production employed dozens of calligraphers, illuminators, painters, and binders over more than a decade.

The tilework alone is one of the great achievements of Islamic decorative art — a technique called **haft rang** (HAHFT RANG, "seven colors") in which polychrome glazes were fired onto large tile panels rather than assembled from small geometric pieces.
